title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing (Figure 3, Physical Obstruction)
description:
Figure 3 (sheet 4 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation): Example of Restricted Sight Distance Due To Physical Obstruction. Plan view of a signalized intersection on a curving arterial. The arterial runs north to south and curves to the right at the top of the sheet. It has a raised, hatched median island that carries shrubs or trees (cloud-shaped symbols with a center dot) and runs through the curve to the intersection, ending in a rounded nose at the stop bar. Dashed lane lines separate the lanes on each side of the median, and a cross street with a double centerline and dashed lane lines crosses the arterial at the intersection box.

Sight lines: Two opposing vehicles are drawn in the curved approach on the far side of the intersection, with measurement leaders running from the vehicles back to the intersection edge. The leaders are labeled 'See Table A for 6.0 sec' (the farther vehicle) and 'See Table A for 5.5 sec' (the nearer vehicle). A left-turning vehicle waits inside the intersection box. Two thin dashed sight lines fan out from it past the planted median, labeled Line A (the left line) and Line B (the right line). The median plantings sit in the sight path and block the view of the opposing traffic between those lines.

Text on the sheet: A note at the lower right says that protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance along Line A is not met and left turns are allowed, and refers the reader to Figure 6 and to Line B distances if the obstruction distance is relatively short. No dimensions in feet are given. The distances are taken from Table A.
notes:
1. Figure 3: Example of restricted sight distance due to physical obstruction.
2. See Table A for 6.0 seconds (sec).
3. See Table A for 5.5 sec.
4. Protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance along Line A is not met and left turns are allowed. See Figure 6 and examine Line B distances if the obstruction distance is relatively short.
5. Sheet 4 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0.
summary: Figure 3 shows a left-turning driver at a signalized intersection whose view of opposing traffic is blocked by planted median islands in a curve. The required sight distances come from Table A for 5.5 and 6.0 second gaps and are checked along Line A. Protected left-turn phasing is required if any minimum distance along Line A is not met, with Line B examined when the obstruction is short.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing (Figure 4, Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Light Opposing Demand)
description:
Figure 4 (sheet 5 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation): Example of Infrequently Restricted Sight Distance Due to Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Light Opposing Left Turn Demand. Plan view of a signalized intersection of a straight arterial (running north to south) with a lower-volume cross street running east to west.

Arterial: A raised hatched median island runs down the center and ends before each intersection. Approaching the intersection, the median bends toward the through lanes at its nose, so each left turn pocket sits to the far side of the opposing pocket, which is a negative offset. The upstream end of the median shows a lateral shift labeled X (a small dimension mark with arrows at the top of the sheet). Dashed lane lines separate the through lanes. A left-turn arrow is drawn in each pocket. In the northbound approach at the bottom, the left-turn lane is shown next to the median nose. A single vehicle is queued in the southbound left turn pocket at the top, labeled 'Generally less than or equal to 2 vehicles per cycle' (shown as the less-than-or-equal symbol).

Intersection box: Two vehicles are shown turning left inside the intersection box, with dashed turning paths curving across it.

Cross street: The cross street at the right is labeled 'Generally less than 10,000 ADT' (average daily traffic).

Text block: A paragraph on the sheet explains the figure's use (see notes).
notes:
1. Figure 4: Example of infrequently restricted sight distance due to negatively offset left turn lanes with light opposing left turn demand.
2. Generally less than or equal to 2 vehicles per cycle (label at the opposing left turn queue).
3. Generally less than 10,000 average daily traffic (ADT) (label at the cross street).
4. This figure is for general use on arterial highways with negatively offset left turn lanes at intersections with lower volume cross streets and/or low volume left turns from the arterial streets. In these situations the queuing from the opposing left turns will be short or infrequent and will usually clear during the cycle, thus resulting in a period of unrestricted sight distance for permissive left turns.
5. Infrequently restricted sight distance generally would be assumed to occur if the cross street has less than 10,000 ADT and opposing left turns are less than two cars per cycle during the peak hour. However, a left turn study may be conducted in place of these guidelines to document the frequency of restricted sight distance. When such a study is conducted, refer to Figure 5.
6. Sheet 5 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0.
summary: Figure 4 illustrates a negatively offset left turn lane arrangement where restricted sight distance happens only infrequently. This applies when the cross street carries less than 10,000 ADT and opposing left turns are fewer than two vehicles per cycle in the peak hour. A left turn study may be used instead, following the Figure 5 method.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing (Figure 5, Frequently Restricted Sight Distance, Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand)
description:
Figure 5 (sheet 6 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation): Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand. Plan view of an arterial intersection (arterial north to south, cross street east to west), with a W and X table at the lower right.

Plan view: A hatched raised median bends at its nose so the left turn pockets are negatively offset. Opposing left-turn pocket at the top holds a queue of vehicles lined up at the stop bar, with a lane width marked W. A vehicle near the middle of the top approach marks the position of the first vehicle in the queue and a vehicle further upstream marks the farthest point. Lateral offset X is dimensioned at the vehicles and at the median shift, and a second W dimension is shown at the pocket width. Sight distance leaders on the left are labeled 'See Table A for 6.0 sec' and 'See Table A for 5.5 sec'. A dashed sight line runs from the waiting left-turn driver past the queue. Inside the intersection box, vehicle positions are dimensioned: the opposing vehicle 5' from the leading edge and 2' lateral offset, a 10' separation between the two left-turning vehicles measured along the sight line, an 8' vehicle length, 2' and 6' lateral dimensions at the lower vehicle, and a dashed 'Turning path for 10' separation' with an angle arc. The bottom approach carries a hatched median nose, left-turn arrow and lane lines.

Cross street label: 'Generally, an Arterial or High Volume Collector Street (10,000 ADT)'.

Table (W and X): W, ft: 9, 10, 11, 12 and X, ft: 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 respectively.

Text block: The paragraphs at the upper right are given in the notes.
notes:
1. Figure 5: Example of frequently restricted sight distance due to negatively offset left turn lanes with moderate opposing left turn demand.
2. See Table A for 6.0 seconds (sec).
3. See Table A for 5.5 sec.
4. Generally, an arterial or high volume collector street (10,000 average daily traffic (ADT)) (label at the cross street).
5. Table, W (ft) and X (ft): W = 9 and X = 1.5; W = 10 and X = 2.0; W = 11 and X = 2.5; W = 12 and X = 3.0.
6. This figure is for general use on arterial highways or high volume collector streets with negatively offset left turn lanes at higher volume cross streets. In these situations, the negative offset, in combination with moderate opposing left turn demand, may result in frequently restricted sight distance for permissive left turns.
7. The determination of frequently restricted sight distance can be determined by: 1) Assessing the frequency of restricted sight distance, and 2) measuring the sight distance. Restricted sight distance will be assumed to occur frequently with moderate opposing left-turn demand if the cross street has more than 10,000 ADT. However, a left turn study may be conducted in place of this guideline to document the actual frequency of restricted sight distance. If the study shows that more than 15% of queues do not clear during their cycles of arrival during the peak hour then restricted visibility is judged to be frequent.
8. The sight distance can be plotted on a striping plan as shown in this figure or as measured in the field. If the sight distance is frequently restricted and is less than the values shown in Table A then remedial action should be taken.
9. Remedial action should first consider removal of the raised median island and restriping to eliminate the negative offset. If this is not feasible then protected left turn phasing is required.
10. Sheet 6 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0.
summary: Figure 5 shows frequently restricted sight distance where negatively offset left turn lanes meet moderate opposing left turn demand on a cross street with more than 10,000 ADT. Restriction is judged frequent if more than 15% of queues do not clear in the peak hour. Where the measured sight distance is below Table A values, the median should first be removed and restriped, and protected phasing is required if that is not feasible.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing (Figure 6, Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand with Right Horizontal Curvature)
description:
Figure 6 (sheet 7 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation): Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand in Combination with Right Horizontal Curvature. Plan view of an arterial intersection where the arterial curves to the right on the upstream (opposing) approach, with a W and X table at the left.

Plan view: The curved approach has a left turn pocket separated from the through lanes by a hatched median (shown as a double line). Several vehicles are lined up in the pocket with lane width W dimensioned at several points and lateral offset X dimensioned at the stop bar and beside the vehicles. Two sight lines are labeled LINE A (defined by the first vehicle in the queue) and LINE B (defined by the last vehicle in an 85th percentile queue). Sight distance leaders drawn around the curve are labeled 'See Table A for 5.5 sec.', 'See Table A for 6.0 sec.', 'See Table A 5.5 sec. maximum' and 'See Table A 6.0 sec. maximum'. Inside the intersection box, the waiting left-turn vehicle is dimensioned with 3' and 1' lateral offsets, 8' vehicle length, a 10' separation to the opposing vehicle, a 1' offset and a 5' dimension at the opposing vehicle, and a dashed 'Turning path for 10' separation'. A left-turn arrow is drawn at the bottom.

Table (W and X): W, ft: 9, 10, 11, 12 and X, ft: 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 respectively.

Text block: The paragraph at the upper left explains Line A, Line B and the queue length estimate (see notes).
notes:
1. Figure 6: Example of frequently restricted sight distance due to moderate opposing left turn demand in combination with right horizontal curvature.
2. Left turning motorists can see downstream of Line A (which is defined by the first vehicle in a queue) and upstream of Line B which is defined by the last vehicle in an 85th percentile queue. They cannot, however, see between Lines A and B. If opposing vehicles can be seen at the required sight distances, shown in Table A, either downstream of Line A or upstream of Line B, then protected left turn phasing is not required. If however, the required sight distances lie between Lines A and B then visibility is inadequate for left turning decisions and protected left turn phasing is required. In the absence of documented observations, the 85th percentile queue length, in feet, is assumed to be 40 V/N, where V equals the peak hour left turn volume and N equals the number of signal cycles per hour.
3. Sight distance leaders: See Table A for 6.0 seconds (sec) maximum. See Table A for 5.5 sec maximum. See Table A for 6.0 sec. See Table A for 5.5 sec.
4. Table, W (ft) and X (ft): W = 9 and X = 1.5; W = 10 and X = 2.0; W = 11 and X = 2.5; W = 12 and X = 3.0.
5. Sheet 7 of 7, Drawing No. S-497.0.
summary: Figure 6 shows how right horizontal curvature combined with moderate opposing left turn demand can restrict sight distance. Line A is set by the first queued vehicle and Line B by the last vehicle of an 85th percentile queue, and drivers cannot see between them. If the Table A distances fall between Lines A and B, protected left turn phasing is required, and the queue is assumed to be 40 V/N feet without observations.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 1 of 12, Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches)
description:
Sheet 1 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections. Approved June 24, 2010 (Rita L. Robinson, General Manager, signed for). Drawn EC, 6-10-10. Sheet caption: Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches to Signalized Jogged Intersections.

Right Jog (upper diagram): Plan view of a jogged intersection where the minor street legs enter the arterial (running east to west) at offset locations, labeled 'Right Jog'. The intersection box is outlined with crosswalks on the west and east sides and short stop-bar crosswalks on the minor street legs. Three vehicles are shown with dashed path lines crossing in the middle of the box, with a circled S symbol, representing a conflict between the opposing left-turning and through paths. A pedestrian pair is shown in the east crosswalk.

Left Jog (lower diagram): Same layout mirrored, labeled 'Left Jog', with the minor street legs offset the other way. A left-turning vehicle with its path and a second vehicle, a circled S, and pedestrians in the east crosswalk are shown.

Bullets beside the Right Jog diagram: pedestrians might not be seen early-on by right-turning motorists, opposing vehicles might not be seen early-on, opposing arterial left turns might interlock. Bullets beside the Left Jog diagram are in the notes.
notes:
1. Right Jog: Pedestrians might not be seen early-on by right-turning motorists. Opposing vehicles might not be seen early-on. Opposing arterial left turns might interlock.
2. Left Jog: Pedestrians might not be seen early-on by left-turning motorists. Opposing vehicles might not be seen early-on. Opposing left turns interlock. Difficult to determine if motorist is making a left turn or jogged through move. So-called opposing moves momentarily can be positioned at approximately right angles to each other.
3. Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches to Signalized Jogged Intersections.
4. To select the most appropriate design for minimizing the above challenges see Sheet 2.
5. The circled S symbol marks the conflict area drawn in each diagram.
summary: Sheet 1 introduces the S-100.0 series on signalized jogged intersections and illustrates the operational problems on the minor street approaches. It shows a right jog and a left jog and lists issues such as pedestrians and opposing vehicles not being seen early and opposing left turns interlocking. It refers the reader to Sheet 2 for selecting a design.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 2 of 12, Design Selection Procedure)
description:
Sheet 2 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation.

Definitions with diagram: Three definitions at the top (see notes) are tied to a schematic plan view of a jogged intersection. A vehicle on the north minor street at left and a vehicle on the south minor street at right are shown. Dashed sight lines run diagonally across the intersection between them, one angle theta 2 (T2) at the left vehicle, measured between the straight-ahead line and the line to the back of the opposing vehicle, and theta 1 (T1) at the right vehicle. X2 is dimensioned along the arterial at the lower left, from the crosswalk or limit line at the far side of the first intersecting leg to the signal pole, and X1 is dimensioned at the upper right the same way. D is dimensioned twice (upper and lower) as the internal storage distance between the hypothetical interior limit lines drawn as vertical lines. Signal poles are drawn with mastarm symbols and heads with arrows.

Selection procedure: A text list gives four steps (see notes). Below it is a note on lighting. No tables.
notes:
1. Theta 1 and theta 2 (symbols T1 and T2) = angle between motorist looking straight ahead and back of opposing vehicle.
2. X1 and X2 = Distance along arterial from the crosswalk line or limit line to the signal pole or BCR at the far side of the first intersecting leg.
3. D = Internal storage distance between real or hypothetical interior limit lines. For minor offset D may be a small or negative number.
4. To select the most appropriate design:
1) Determine if there is a Left Jog or a Right Jog. See Sheets 3, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11 for left jogged intersections and Sheets 4, 6, 8 and 12 for right jogged intersections.
2) Determine D. If D is 40' or more then interior limit lines are required. If D is less than 40' then the jog is operated as a single intersection. See Sheets 10, 11 and 12 for intersections with interior limit lines and Sheets 3 through 9 for single intersection operation.
3) Determine theta 1 and theta 2. If theta 1 or theta 2 is greater than 20 degrees and D is less than 40' then some form of opposed phasing is required for the minor street. See Sheets 7 through 9 for situations requiring opposed phasing. See Sheets 3 through 6 for situations for which concurrent phasing is adequate. Note that for Sheets 4 and 6 opposed phasing is required if diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, due to the unexpected presence of pedestrians crossing the path of right-turning motorists.
4) Determine X1 and X2. If X1 and X2 are 50' or more and D is less than 40' then only internal mastarms are to be used on the arterial street. If X1 and X2 are less than 50' then only external mastarms are to be used on the arterial street. See Sheets 3, 4, 7, and 8 for internal mastarm designs and Sheets 5, 6 and 9 for external mastarm designs.
5. Note: The drawings on Sheets 3 through 12 are not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
6. 'BCR' is as printed. The printed text of step 4 reads 'X1 and X' in the less than 50' condition (apparently X2).
summary: Sheet 2 defines the geometry terms theta 1, theta 2, X1, X2 and D and gives a four-step procedure to pick among the jogged intersection designs on Sheets 3 through 12. The choice depends on left or right jog, internal distance D against 40 ft, sight angles against 20 degrees, and X distances against 50 ft.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 3 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms)
description:
Sheet 3 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection of an arterial running east to west with a minor street entering from the north on one side and the south on the other. The north leg has a left-turn arrow and dashed lane lines, and the south leg has an opposite left-turn arrow. Hypothetical interior limit lines are not drawn, and the intersection operates as one. Dimension X2 is shown at the left between the north stop line and the far-side signal pole, and X1 at the right at the south side. Dashed sight cones show angles theta 1 and theta 2 between opposing vehicles on the minor street (one vehicle at the lower left and one at the upper right). A curved dashed line labeled R=30' min. crosses the intersection box diagonally and marks the opposing left turn paths.

Signal equipment: Mastarms and signal heads are labeled with phase numbers and sizes: phase 2 and phase 4 and phase 6 and phase 8 arrows at the poles, pedestrian signal heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P, accessible pedestrian signals (APS), and R9-3a'S signs (read as R9-3a) with the label 'WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC' with a leader at each corner pole. Internal mastarm poles stand inside the intersection box.

Phase diagram (lower right): A table of eight boxes numbered 1 to 8. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out (unused). Box 2 shows a solid arrow and a dashed arrow in the north-south directions (southbound, with a dashed opposite direction). Box 4 shows a solid arrow westbound with a dashed double arrow. Box 6 shows a solid arrow northbound with a dashed arrow. Box 8 shows a solid arrow eastbound with a dashed double arrow.

Notes on the right: see notes.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 >= 50'.
2. The beveled visors shown should be installed only where cross-traffic motorists would see 50% or more of the lens area of a far-side signal as they wait at the limit line. PV heads should be used if beveled visors would not be adequate.
3. Labels on the drawing: WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC; R9-3a'S; R=30' min.; APS (accessible pedestrian signal); 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P (pedestrian heads); phases 2, 4, 6, 8.
4. Sheet 3 of 12.
summary: Sheet 3 shows the signal layout for a left jogged intersection with internal mastarms. It applies where D is under 40 ft, both sight angles are 20 degrees or less, and X1 and X2 are 50 ft or more. It shows pedestrian heads, APS, R9-3a signs, WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC and an 8-phase diagram using phases 2, 4, 6 and 8.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 4 of 12, Right Jogged Intersection, Prohibited Left Turn)
description:
Sheet 4 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Right jogged Intersection, Prohibited Left Turn.

Plan view: A right-jogged intersection with the arterial and minor street legs offset. The north leg has a left-turn arrow and the south leg has a median island with curved nose and hatch lines. Diagonal crosswalks cross the intersection from the northwest to the southeast and are shown as two parallel diagonal lines and labeled 15' MIN. (width). Signs R3-2 (no left turn) are shown near the left-turn paths at the northwest and east poles, and a vertical label R/C is marked beside a heavy line at the lower left. Dimensions: X2 on the left and X1 on the right, RCR=30' MIN. at the center along the diagonal, with theta 1 and theta 2 sight angles shown by dashed lines between opposing vehicles. Signal heads and APS units at corners are labeled 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with phases 2, 4, 6 and 8 arrows, and 'WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC' signs at the west and east poles.

Phase diagram (lower right): Eight boxes numbered 1 to 8. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid arrow southbound and a dashed arrow beside it, box 4 shows a dashed double arrow with a solid westbound arrow, box 6 shows a solid northbound arrow and dashed arrows, box 8 shows solid eastbound with dashed double arrows.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 and theta 2 <=20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 >=50'; and d) Diagonal crosswalks are feasible.
2. Where diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, use opposed phasing, as shown on Sheet 8.
3. The treatment to allow arterial left turns in one direction and prohibited in the other direction is an operational option. For other typical left turn operations on the arterial street see Sheets 6 and 8.
4. The beveled visors shown should be installed only where cross-traffic motorists would see 50% or more of the lens area of a far-side signal as they wait at the limit line. PV heads should be used if beveled visors would not be adequate.
5. Labels on the drawing: WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC; R3-2; RCR=30' MIN.; 15' MIN.; R/C; APS; 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P; phases 2, 4, 6, 8.
6. Sheet 4 of 12.
summary: Sheet 4 shows a right jogged intersection with diagonal crosswalks and a prohibited left turn (R3-2) in one direction. It applies where D is under 40 ft, both angles are 20 degrees or less, X1 and X2 are at least 50 ft and diagonal crosswalks are feasible. Otherwise opposed phasing from Sheet 8 is used.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 5 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, External Mastarms)
description:
Sheet 5 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, External Mastarms.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection of an arterial (east to west) with the minor street offset: the north leg has a left-turn arrow and dashed lane lines, the south leg has the opposing left-turn arrow. Hypothetical interior limit lines are not drawn and the intersection operates as one. X2 is dimensioned on the left side between the north limit line and the far-side pole, and X1 on the right side. Dashed sight lines at theta 1 (upper) and theta 2 (lower) are drawn between two minor street vehicles, with a dashed curve labeled R=30' min. across the intersection. Signal poles are at the outside corners (external mastarms) with signal heads, arrows and labels: phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P, APS at the corner poles, R9-3a'S signs (as printed) with the label WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC at the west and east corner poles.

Phase diagram: a table of eight numbered boxes in two rows of four. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2: a solid downward arrow with a dashed upward arrow. Box 4: a solid left arrow with a dashed double-headed arrow. Box 6: a solid upward arrow with a dashed downward arrow. Box 8: a solid right arrow with a dashed double-headed arrow.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 <50'.
2. Labels on the drawing: WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC; R9-3a'S; R=30' min.; APS (accessible pedestrian signal); 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P (pedestrian signal heads); phases 2, 4, 6 and 8.
3. Left jogged Intersection, External Mastarms.
4. Sheet 5 of 12.
summary: Sheet 5 shows the signal layout for a left jogged intersection using external mastarms, for cases with D under 40 ft, both sight angles 20 degrees or less and X1 and X2 under 50 ft. It includes pedestrian heads, APS and WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC signs with a four-phase (2, 4, 6, 8) diagram.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 6 of 12, Right Jogged Intersection, Protected Left Turn)
description:
Sheet 6 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Right jogged Intersection, Protected Left Turn.

Plan view: A right-jogged intersection of an arterial with the minor street offset and a pair of diagonal crosswalks running across the intersection from the northwest to the southeast (two parallel diagonal bands). The north leg has a left-turn arrow and the south leg has a left-turn arrow in a lane next to a double yellow median. X2 is dimensioned on the left and X1 on the right. Dashed sight lines at theta 1 and theta 2 are drawn between minor street vehicles. Signal poles are external (at the corners) with heads and arrows labeled phases 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P, APS units, and WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC labels at the west and east poles. Phase 5 is a protected left turn arrow shown at the south side poles, with multi-arrow symbols.

Phase diagram: a table of eight numbered boxes in two rows of four. Boxes 1, 3 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2: solid downward arrow and dashed upward arrow. Box 4: solid left arrow with dashed double-headed arrow. Box 5: a curved arrow turning from north to east (a protected left turn). Box 6: solid upward arrow with dashed downward arrow. Box 8: solid right arrow with dashed double-headed arrow.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 <50'; and d) Diagonal crosswalks are feasible.
2. Where diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, use opposed phasing, as shown on Sheet 8.
3. If arterial left turns are to be allowed in both directions, at least one direction shall have protected left turns, as shown. For other typical left turn options on the arterial street see Sheets 4 and 8.
4. Labels on the drawing: WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC; APS; 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P; phases 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8.
5. Sheet 6 of 12.
summary: Sheet 6 shows a right jogged intersection with diagonal crosswalks, external mastarms and a protected left turn (phase 5) in one arterial direction. It applies where D is under 40 ft, both angles are 20 degrees or less, X1 and X2 are under 50 ft and diagonal crosswalks are feasible.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 7 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms/Opposed Phasing)
description:
Sheet 7 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms/Opposed Phasing.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection of an arterial (east to west) with minor street legs offset. The north leg has a left-turn arrow and the south leg has an opposing left-turn arrow. Dimension X2 is shown at the left and X1 at the right, and D (internal storage distance between the interior limit lines) is dimensioned at the right, between the north and south minor street legs. Dashed sight lines at theta 1 and theta 2 run between the opposing minor street vehicles. 'KEEP CLEAR' pavement markings are drawn in the intersection between the cross street legs (rotated copies of the text reading KEEP and CLEAR in four positions). Signal poles with internal mastarms carry heads and arrows labeled phases 2, 3, 4 and 6, pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P, 6P, APS and R9-3a'S signs at the corner poles.

Phase diagrams (lower right, three tables): The first table, with no caption, then 'Alternate 1' and 'Alternate 2'. Each has eight boxes. Main table: box 1 crossed; box 2 solid downward arrow with dashed upward arrow; box 3 solid right arrow with a curved arrow veering up and right, and a dashed left arrow; box 4 dashed right arrow, a solid left arrow, and a curved arrow veering down-left; boxes 5, 7 and 8 crossed; box 6 solid upward arrow with dashed downward arrow. Alternate 1: boxes 1, 5 and 7 crossed; box 2 same as main; box 3 solid right arrow with curved arrow veering up and right; box 4 solid left arrow with dashed double arrow; box 6 same as main; box 8 dashed double arrow. Alternate 2: boxes 1, 5 and 7 crossed; box 2 same as main; box 3 solid left arrow with curved arrow veering down-left; box 4 solid right arrow with dashed double arrow; box 6 same as main; box 8 dashed double arrow.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 or theta 2 >20 degrees.
2. The alternate signal phasing schemes shown below, with corresponding signal head modifications (not shown), should be used only where the intersection would be operating near capacity with the more conventional opposed phasing. Generally, the alternate phasing would be necessary where pedestrian calls occur on most cycles. Where used, the lighter volume side street approach should have the left arrow indications. If one or both of the crosswalks across the arterial street can be eliminated, then the intersection operation can have more efficient phasing than shown.
3. Where D>=20', "KEEP CLEAR" pavement markings should be installed between the cross street legs, as shown.
4. Labels on the drawing: R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 3P, 4P, 6P; phases 2, 3, 4 and 6; Alternate 1; Alternate 2.
5. Sheet 7 of 12.
summary: Sheet 7 shows a left jogged intersection with internal mastarms and opposed phasing, used where D is under 40 ft and a sight angle exceeds 20 degrees. KEEP CLEAR markings go between the cross street legs when D is 20 ft or more. Alternate phasing 1 and 2 are for near-capacity operation with frequent pedestrian calls.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 8 of 12, Right Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms/Opposed Phasing)
description:
Sheet 8 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Right Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms, Opposed Phasing.

Plan view: A right-jogged intersection of an arterial with minor street legs offset. The north leg has a left-turn arrow in an 18' min. wide painted median pocket, drawn as a curved double line, and the south leg has a matching left-turn pocket marked 18' min. (cat-tracked, side by side left-turn lanes). 9' min. dimensions are marked twice (above and below) between dashed vehicle path lines in the intersection. X2 is dimensioned on the left and X1 on the right. Dashed sight lines at theta 1 and theta 2 run between minor street vehicles. Internal mastarm poles carry signal heads with arrows labeled phases 2, 3, 4 and 6, pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P, 6P, APS units and R9-3a'S signs at the corners.

Phase diagrams (lower right, three tables): the main table, then 'Alternate 1' and 'Alternate 2'. Main table: box 1 crossed; box 2 solid downward arrow with dashed upward arrow; box 3 dashed left-right arrow above a solid right arrow that curves down-right; box 4 solid left arrow with a curved arrow veering up-left, and a dashed double arrow; boxes 5, 7 and 8 crossed; box 6 solid upward arrow with dashed downward arrow. Alternate 1: box 3 solid right arrow curving down-right; box 4 solid left arrow with dashed double arrow; box 8 dashed double arrow; boxes 1, 5 and 7 crossed. Alternate 2: box 3 solid left arrow with curved arrow veering up-left; box 4 dashed double arrow with solid right arrow; box 8 dashed double arrow; boxes 1, 5 and 7 crossed.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 or theta 2 >20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 >= 50'.
2. The arterial, cat-tracked side-by-side left-turn lanes, as shown, are possible only where the painted median channelization is at least 18' wide. For other typical left turn options on the arterial street see Sheets 4 and 6.
3. The alternate signal phasing schemes shown below with corresponding signal head modifications should be used only where the intersection would be operating near capacity with the more conventional opposed phasing. Generally, the alternate phasing would be necessary where pedestrian calls occur on most cycles. Where used, the lighter volume side street approach should have the right arrow indications. If one or both of the crosswalks across the arterial street can be eliminated, then the intersection operation can have more efficient phasing than shown.
4. Where D>=20' "KEEP CLEAR" pavement markings should be installed between the cross street legs, as shown in Sheet 7.
5. Labels on the drawing: 18' min.; 9' min.; R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 3P, 4P, 6P; phases 2, 3, 4 and 6; Alternate 1; Alternate 2.
6. Sheet 8 of 12.
summary: Sheet 8 shows a right jogged intersection with internal mastarms and opposed phasing, with cat-tracked side-by-side left turn lanes where the painted median is at least 18 ft wide. It applies where D is under 40 ft, a sight angle exceeds 20 degrees and X1 and X2 are 50 ft or more, with two alternate phasing schemes.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 9 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, External Mastarms/Opposed Phasing)
description:
Sheet 9 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, External Mastarms/Opposed Phasing.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection of an arterial with offset minor street legs. The north leg has a left-turn arrow and the south leg has the opposing left-turn arrow. X2 is dimensioned on the left and X1 on the right. Dashed sight lines at theta 1 and theta 2 run between the opposing minor street vehicles. Signal poles are at the outside corners (external mastarms) with heads and arrows labeled phases 2, 3, 4 and 6, pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P and 6P, APS units, and R9-3a'S signs.

Phase diagram: a table of eight numbered boxes in two rows of four. Boxes 1, 5, 7 and 8 are crossed out. Box 2: solid downward arrow with dashed upward arrow. Box 3: solid right arrow with a curved arrow veering up and right, and a dashed left arrow. Box 4: dashed right arrow and a solid left arrow with a curved arrow veering down-left. Box 6: solid upward arrow with dashed downward arrow.
notes:
1. Install where: a) D<40'; and b) theta 1 or theta 2 >20 degrees; and c) X1 and X2 <50'.
2. See Sheet 7 for alternate signal phasing schemes.
3. Labels on the drawing: R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 3P, 4P, 6P; phases 2, 3, 4 and 6.
4. Sheet 9 of 12.
summary: Sheet 9 shows a left jogged intersection with external mastarms and opposed phasing, for D under 40 ft, a sight angle over 20 degrees and X1 and X2 under 50 ft. Alternate phasing schemes are on Sheet 7.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 10 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines)
description:
Sheet 10 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection of an arterial where the two minor street legs are far enough apart that the jog is operated as two intersections. The north leg has a left-turn arrow with a double line and dashed lane lines. A raised, curved median nose is drawn in the south leg between the two internal approaches. D is dimensioned at the left between the interior limit lines of the arterial segment. Signal poles carry heads and arrows labeled phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P, APS units and R9-3a'S signs at the corner poles. The lower approach has a left-turn arrow and lane lines, with phase 2 and phase 8 heads at the lower corners.

Phase diagram: a table of eight numbered boxes in two rows of four. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2: solid downward arrow with dashed upward arrow. Box 4: solid left arrow with dashed double-headed arrow. Box 6: solid upward arrow with dashed downward arrow. Box 8: solid right arrow with dashed double-headed arrow.
notes:
1. Install where D>=40'.
2. Labels on the drawing: R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P; phases 2, 4, 6 and 8.
3. Left jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines.
4. Sheet 10 of 12.
summary: Sheet 10 shows a left jogged intersection with interior limit lines, used where D is 40 ft or more. It shows the signal head layout with phases 2, 4, 6 and 8 and the corresponding four-phase diagram.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 11 of 12, Left Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines, Slot Clearance)
description:
Sheet 11 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Left jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines, Slot Clearance.

Plan view: A left-jogged intersection with interior limit lines (D dimensioned at the left) and added overlap and clearance signal heads. A row of small circles across the top of the intersection marks the interior limit line, with labels OLA PV CUT-OFF, OLB, and PV (G,R only), and a second row of circles across the bottom labeled OLA, PV (G,R only), OLB PV CUT-OFF. The north leg has a left-turn arrow and the south leg has a median nose. Signal poles carry heads labeled phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8, OLA and OLB overlap indications, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P, APS units and R9-3a'S signs. Phase 1 and 5 left turn arrows are shown with multi-arrow symbols.

Phase diagram (lower right): Eight boxes in two rows of four. Box 1 is split by a dashed line with a left-turn arrow in the lower half. Box 2 is split by a dashed line: a downward arrow above, and below it an upward dashed arrow with a downward solid arrow and the label OLA. Box 3 is crossed out. Box 4: dashed right arrow with a solid left arrow. Box 5: a curved arrow turning from north to east in the upper half and empty lower half. Box 6: labeled OLB with an upward arrow and dashed down arrow in the upper half, and an upward arrow in the lower half. Box 7 is crossed out. Box 8: solid right arrow with dashed double-headed arrow. Caption below: OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
notes:
1. Install where: a) 40'<=D<=200' and b) There have been 4 or more Right Angle accidents or 4 or more Left Turn accidents in a recent 12 month period at one of the intersections involving vehicles departing from the interior limit line.
2. OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
3. Labels on the drawing: OLA PV CUT-OFF; OLB PV CUT-OFF; PV (G,R only); OLA; OLB; R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P; phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8.
4. Sheet 11 of 12.
summary: Sheet 11 shows a left jogged intersection with interior limit lines and slot clearance overlap phases (OLA and OLB). It is for D between 40 ft and 200 ft where there have been 4 or more right angle or left turn accidents in 12 months involving vehicles departing from the interior limit line.

title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 12 of 12, Right Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines)
description:
Sheet 12 of 12, Drawing No. S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Caption: Right jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines.

Plan view: A right-jogged intersection of an arterial with interior limit lines. D is dimensioned at the left. Rows of small circles mark the interior limit lines at the top and bottom of the intersection, with labels OLA PV CUT-OFF, OLB, PV (G,R only), OLA and OLB PV CUT-OFF. The north leg has a left-turn pocket with a curved median nose and the south leg has a back-to-back left-turn pocket, drawn as an S-shaped curve through the intersection with left-turn arrows in opposite directions. Signal poles carry heads labeled phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, OLA and OLB overlap indications, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P, APS and R9-3a'S signs.

Phase diagram (lower right): Eight boxes in two rows of four. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 is split by a dashed line: above it a solid downward arrow with a dashed upward arrow, below it a downward arrow labeled OLA. Box 4: dashed right arrow with solid left arrow. Box 6 is split by a dashed line: above it an upward arrow labeled OLB, below it an upward arrow with a dashed downward arrow. Box 8: solid right arrow with dashed double-headed arrow. Caption below: OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
notes:
1. Install where 40'<=D<=200'.
2. Mask only the Green and Red lenses of the PV heads.
3. The back-to-back left-turn lanes, as shown, are possible only where D>=70'. Where not possible, a left-turn lane in one direction, possibly with a left-turn restriction in the other direction, should be considered.
4. OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
5. Labels on the drawing: OLA PV CUT-OFF; OLB PV CUT-OFF; PV (G,R only); OLA; OLB; R9-3a'S; APS; 2P, 4P, 6P, 8P; phases 2, 4, 6 and 8.
6. Sheet 12 of 12.
summary: Sheet 12 shows a right jogged intersection with interior limit lines and overlap phases OLA and OLB for D from 40 ft to 200 ft. Back-to-back left-turn lanes are possible only where D is 70 ft or more. Only the green and red lenses of the PV heads are masked.

title: Street Name Sign Posting (Sheet 2 of 4, Jogged Intersection Offset X)
description:
Sheet 2 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Title: STREET NAME SIGN POSTING.

Upper diagram, 'When X is less than 100'': Plan view of an offset (jogged) intersection. "D" AVENUE is the minor street, with its north leg entering on the left and its south leg offset to the right, and "A" STREET (labeled "A" at the left and STREET at the right) runs east to west between the two legs. A dimension X is drawn along the north side between the west curb line of the east leg and the sign post location on the right. Each corner has a thin sidewalk line parallel to the curb. Street name sign posts are shown as short thick bars with a dot at the end of the post. Posts are placed at the northwest corner of the north leg, at the west side on the south curb line of "A" street, at the north curb at the right end of dimension X, and at the southeast corner of the south leg.

Lower diagram, 'When X is 100' or Greater': The same offset intersection with the dimension X marked again. The layout shows the same sign posts as the upper diagram plus additional posts, so that a sign is placed at each of the corners on both legs of the jog: posts at the near corner of the north leg, near and far ends of dimension X on the north curb, the south side of "A" street, and the south leg corners.

No other dimensions or notes appear on this sheet.
notes:
1. When X is less than 100'.
2. When X is 100' or Greater.
3. Labels on the drawing: "D" AVENUE; "A" STREET; dimension X.
4. Sheet 2 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3.
summary: Sheet 2 shows where street name signs are posted at an offset (jogged) intersection, depending on the offset distance X. When X is less than 100 ft fewer posts are used than when X is 100 ft or greater, as shown in the two plan diagrams.

title: Street Name Sign Posting (Sheet 3 of 4, Street Name Signs for Streets Adjoining Divided Roads and Service Roads)
description:
Sheet 3 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Title: STREET NAME SIGN POSTING.

Plan view: A schematic of side streets meeting a major street that has parallel service roads, with the plan drawn at the upper left through the lower right. Side streets labeled "F" St., "G" St., "H", "I" St. run in from the left and end in rounded curb returns at the service road. A narrow raised island (a rounded elongated outline) lies alongside the service road. Labels read Street, Rd. and Service along the roads, and a one-way arrow marks the traffic direction on each service road: a downward arrow on the left service road (Rd., Service) and an upward arrow on the right service road (Rd., Service). The main road in the middle carries "A" (labeled "A" with Street on the right side). Street name sign posts are shown as short thick bars with a dot at the end. Posts are placed at the corner of "F" St. at the top left, at both corners of the "G" St. and "H" side streets where they meet the service road, and along each island at about equal spacing (at both ends and one in the middle) and at the corner of "I" St. Right side: a corner at the upper right and lower right (labeled Street) each have posts at the curb return.

No dimensions or notes are shown.
notes:
1. Labels on the drawing: "F" St.; "G" St.; "H" St.; "I" St.; "A" Street; Service Rd. (left and right, one-way arrows shown); Street.
2. Sheet 3 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3.
summary: Sheet 3 shows street name sign post locations where side streets intersect a street with one-way service roads and raised islands. Posts sit at the curb returns of the side streets and along the islands beside the service roads.

title: Street Name Sign Posting (Sheet 4 of 4, Street Name Signs at Service Roads, Dimension Y)
description:
Sheet 4 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Title: STREET NAME SIGN POSTING.

Plan view: A continuation of the service road layout from Sheet 3. Side streets "J" St., "K" St., "L" St., "M" St. and "N" St. run in from the left and end at rounded curb returns beside the service road. A raised island labeled Street lies along the upper service road with sign posts at both ends and in the middle. Two-way service road arrows (a downward arrow and an upward arrow) are shown at the left center, labeled Rd. Service road labels are Rd. and Service, and "A" is labeled at the lower right of the arterial. Posts are drawn at the corners of each side street's curb returns (two for "K", "L", "M" St. at the service road, one at "J" St.) and several posts are spaced along the island and the service road edge.

Dimension Y: Dimension Y is drawn at the bottom, between the curb line of "M"/"N" St. and the service road, near the curb return of "N" St. At the lower left, two posts sit on the north curb of "N" St. A callout with an arrow points at the right-hand post: 'Omit this sign when Y is less than 100''.
notes:
1. Omit this sign when Y is less than 100' (callout pointing to the post at the "N" St. curb return near the service road).
2. Labels on the drawing: "J" St.; "K" St.; "L" St.; "M" St.; "N" St.; "A"; Street; Service Rd. (one-way arrows shown); dimension Y.
3. Sheet 4 of 4, Drawing No. S-221.3.
summary: Sheet 4 shows street name sign posting for side streets and service roads, including the rule to omit one sign when dimension Y is less than 100 ft. It continues the plan view from Sheet 3.
